claims.body: On shot suppression, Dallas is one of the league’s best, but Nashville is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Expect the Predators to give up the bigger pile of shots.

story.head: The Stars are rolling
paras: The Predators won the teams’ first meeting this season, 2-1 in Nashville on Oct 3. The Stars have won four straight, while the Predators (11-6-5) lost 7-3 to Minnesota on Nov 17. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Predators fourth (tied for 12th in the NHL) and the Stars second (tied for eighth).

The Predators’ record (.614) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.530), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games. So is the Stars’ (.682 on chances worth .602), largely because they’re 8-4 in one-goal games.

This season, the Stars have outscored teams 62-54, even though they’ve been outscored 40-39 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 13-9, and no team creates more chances on the power play.

The Predators keep things calm after the whistle (2nd lowest), play some of the league’s fastest games (3rd) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (31st). The Stars, by contrast, play slow, tight games (lowest). They also take more penalties than they draw (32nd). They also block more shots than anyone (1st), so the Stars are likely to get in the way of a lot of the Predators’ shots. Dallas has allowed 2.45 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. The Stars keep shots away, but the Preds give up plenty.

Filip Forsberg (8 G / 16 A / 24 P in 22 GP) leads the Predators in scoring, and Steven Stamkos (12 G / 11 A / 23 P in 22 GP) has a team-high twelve goals. For the Stars, Mikko Rantanen (10 G / 17 A / 27 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring. Jason Robertson (10 G / 16 A / 26 P in 22 GP) is next in line, with seven points in his last five games.

Jake Oettinger (12-4-1 / .901 SV% in 17 GS) will likely start for Dallas. Nashville has two options in net: Juuse Saros (7-4-4 / .918 SV% in 15 GS) and Justus Annunen (4-2-0 / .862 SV% in 6 GS). Saros has started six of their last ten games, but Annunen got the last one on Nov 17. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
